newsitem.title: MALTA: MALTA TRADE GAP WIDENS BY 4.5 PERCENT IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: MALTA TRADE GAP WIDENS BY 4.5 PERCENT IN 1996.

text.p: Malta saw its trade gap widen by 4.5 percent in 1996 as exports dropped at a faster rate than imports compared with the previous year, the Central Office of Statistics reported on Monday.

Imports fell by 27.2 million Maltese pounds, or 2.6 percent, to 1.01 billion ($2.6 billion) in 1996 compared to the previous year. Fewer consumer goods were imported, down by 17.9 million pounds, or 7.6 percent, to 218.3 million, the office said.
Imports of industrial supplies rose marginally by 3.1 million to 624.4 million, but total capital goods were worth 167.8 million.

Domestic exports went down by 58.1 million or 9.2 per cent to L571.6 million, re-exports increased by 14.7 million to reach 59.9 million, resulting in a trade gap that widened by 16.2 million or 4.5 per cent to 379.0 million. ($1= 0.38 Maltese pound)
